headline: Vol got cheap and semis went vertical on the Micron/Korea chip impulse — while equal-weight versus the index printed a 52-week low, so the tape just narrowed back to one trade.
summary: Yesterday's participation broke was a one-day event. Today SPX +0.8% and NDX +1.1% were bought almost entirely through the AI complex: SOXX +2.8% (+18.2% on the month, z=1.55, acc 1.38), SMH +2.5% (+15.1%), TSM +3.0%, ASML +3.3%, AVGO +3.3%, AMD +2.5% (+38.1% on the month, z=1.90, acc 1.76), NVDA +2.2% at the 100th percentile. Asia carried it first — Nikkei +3.30% to 68,957 (+5.3% on the week) on a chip-led melt-up after Micron's print and Korean export data, EWT +2.9%, EWY +2.8%, KOSPI +1.9%, TWII at the 100th percentile. The cost is internals: RSP/SPY fell another 0.4%, now z=-2.11, -4.5% on the month, at the 3.6th percentile of 52 weeks — worse than yesterday's z=-1.91. IWM/SPY is -4.8% on the month. QQQ/SPY z=1.93, SMH/SPY z=1.94 with acceleration 1.53, high-beta/low-vol at the 100th percentile. Narrowness is accelerating, not resolving.

The rates shock paused again rather than reversed. MOVE fell 1.8% to 106.17, a second straight drop, and the rates composite improved from -78 to -76 — but the level is unchanged and still punitive: 10y 5.24% (96th percentile), 30y 5.61% (97th), 10y real 2.88% with z=1.72 and acceleration 1.39, 30-year mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile and +62bp on the month. TLT sits at the 1st percentile of the year, IEF -3.0% on the month. Equity vol, meanwhile, is priced as if none of that exists: VIX -4.6% to 15.64 (12th percentile), VIX3M 18.23 (7th percentile), term structure -2.7%, SKEW -4.3% on the month. Credit stayed cooperative — HYG +0.1%, HYG/IEF +0.3% at the 94th percentile, BKLN at the 92nd — pushing the credit & vol composite from 26 to 42 and the risk regime from -13 to -10. So the improvement today is in volatility and credit, not in the discount rate.

The dollar stopped going up (DXY -0.1% to 101.95, still 97th percentile, z=1.19) and that was enough for EEM +1.0% and a bounce in offshore beta, but the peso did not get the memo: USDMXN +0.7% to 18.201, z=2.72 with acceleration 2.20, still the most extreme reading on the board, and EWW is -8.1% on the month with relative strength -8.9%. USDBRL +0.9%, USDINR at the 94th percentile with Sensex at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks and INDA -7.0% on the month. AUDJPY z=-1.78. The dollar pause is a reprieve, not a turn.

Underneath, two liquidations keep running. Hard assets: gold -0.9% to 4,166 (-5.6% on the month, acc -2.01), silver -6.7% on the month, GDX acceleration -2.71, GDXJ -2.64, NEM -2.57, REMX -17.5% at the 1st percentile, NLR -12.1% at the 0.3rd percentile, URA -10.1%. Copper is the exception and it matters: +1.0%, COPX +2.0%, FCX +3.7%, copper/gold +1.9% at the 95th percentile with acceleration 1.44 — growth, not inflation. And the rate-sensitive consumer is being taken apart with no defensive hiding place: NKE -4.9% to the 0th percentile, MCD z=-2.36 at the 1st, HD -10.3% on the month at the 1st, XRT/SPY at the 3rd, XHB/SPY at the 1.3rd, NFLX -18.8% on the month at the 0th. Staples and low-vol offered nothing either — XLP -5.5%, SPLV -5.0%, XLU -6.1% on the month. Financials remain in open liquidation despite a 98th-percentile 3m10y curve: XLF -7.1% on the month, BX -16.9%, GS -10.3%, IAI -7.6%, KIE z=-1.81.

good.text: Semis went vertical on the Micron/Korea chip impulse: SOXX +2.8% (+18.2% on the month, acc 1.38), SMH +2.5%, TSM +3.0%, ASML +3.3%, AMD +2.5% and +38.1% on the month, NVDA at the 100th percentile.

Volatility and credit both improved: VIX -4.6% to 15.64 (12th percentile), VIX3M at the 7th, HYG/IEF +0.3% at the 94th percentile, BKLN at the 92nd. Credit & vol composite 26 to 42; risk regime -13 to -10.
Bond vol kept bleeding lower for a second day — MOVE -1.8% to 106.17 — and the rates composite ticked from -78 to -76, the first consecutive improvement of the move.
Copper/gold +1.9% to the 95th percentile with acceleration 1.44, copper +1.0%, COPX +2.0%, FCX +3.7% — the hard-asset liquidation is precious metals, not industrial demand.
Asia tech led the world: Nikkei +3.30% to 68,957 (+5.3% week, relative strength turning up), EWT +2.9%, EWY +2.8% (+7.0% on the month), KOSPI +1.9%, with USDKRW -0.9%.
Crypto is quietly re-leading: BTC +10.1% on the month to 85,118, ETH +12.5%, SOL +19.1%, MSTR +29.4%, IBIT +10.0% — all turning up with positive 1m relative strength.

bad.text: Breadth made a new low versus the index: RSP/SPY -0.4% today, z=-2.11, -4.5% on the month, 3.6th percentile of 52 weeks — worse than yesterday. IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month. Yesterday's participation bounce is gone.

The level of rates never healed: 10y 5.24% (96th pctile), 30y 5.61% (97th), 10y real 2.88% with acceleration 1.39, 30-year mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile. TLT at the 1st percentile of the year.
Equity vol at the 12th percentile against MOVE still +33.2% on the month (z=1.78) and SKEW -4.3% — crash protection is cheapening into the widest rates/equity vol gap of the quarter.
The consumer is cracking with no defensive offset: NKE -4.9% (0th pctile), MCD z=-2.36 (1st), HD -10.3% on the month (1st), NFLX -18.8% (0th), while XLP -5.5%, XLU -6.1% and SPLV -5.0% on the month.

Peso stress is still the most extreme print on the board — USDMXN z=2.72, acceleration 2.20 — with EWW -8.1% on the month and MXX rolling over; India (Sensex 0th pctile, INDA -7.0%) and China (FXI -2.3%, KWEB 1st pctile) are the other EM casualties.

Hard-asset and power liquidation is still the fastest-moving thing: GDX acceleration -2.71, GDXJ -2.64, NEM -2.57, gold -5.6% on the month, REMX -17.5% (1st pctile), NLR -12.1% (0th), CEG -12.6%, VST at the 4th pctile.

trades.name: Long semis vs short equal-weight
trades.line: Long SMH / short RSP — narrowness is accelerating, not fading
trades.expr: Buy SMH (or SOXX), short RSP in equal dollars, ~1.0x beta-adjusted; or buy SMH 3-month 25-delta calls funded by RSP downside.
trades.thesis: The index is being carried by one theme. SMH/SPY z=1.94 with acceleration 1.53 and SOXX +18.2% on the month, against RSP/SPY at the 3.6th percentile of 52 weeks. With 10y real yields at z=1.72 the median S&P name has no multiple support while the AI capex complex has its own earnings cycle (Micron, Korean exports). Own the leadership and fund it with the thing that keeps making new relative lows.
trades.trigger: Today: SOXX +2.8%, SMH +2.5%, TSM +3.0%, ASML +3.3% while RSP/SPY fell another 0.4% to a new 52-week relative low and its z deteriorated from -1.91 to -2.11.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY reclaims its 200-day (currently 4.4% above spot) or SMH/SPY closes below its 50-day with acceleration flipping negative.
trades.target: Another 8-10% on the ratio; SMH/SPY from 0.823 toward 0.89.

trades.name: Short housing at a 100th-percentile mortgage rate
trades.line: Short ITB/XHB — 7.28% mortgage, builders at 1st pctile rel
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy 3-month ITB/XHB put spreads ~10% out of the money; pair with short DHI and short HD for the renovation leg.
trades.thesis: The 30-year mortgage is at 7.28%, the 100th percentile of the year and +62bp on the month, with the 10y real yield at 2.88% and still accelerating (acc 1.39). Builder incentives are already capping margins; ITB is -14.7% over three months, -9.7% below its 200-day, and XHB/SPY sits at the 1.3rd percentile. Even a 5bp-per-day rally in rates has not bought the group a single bid.
trades.trigger: ITB -0.4% today on a +0.8% SPX tape, DHI -0.7%, HD -10.3% on the month at the 1st percentile, while the mortgage rate refused to come off its highs.
trades.stop: 10y back below 5.00% / mortgage under 7.00% with ITB reclaiming its 200-day.
trades.target: ITB -10% to -12% from 87; XHB/SPY to new lows.

trades.name: Electrical equipment over power generators
trades.line: Long ETN+GRID / short CEG+NLR — picks over the power price
trades.expr: Long 50% ETN / 50% GRID against short 50% CEG / 50% NLR, dollar neutral.
trades.thesis: AI electrification spend is still being paid for in equipment, not in merchant power. ETN is +12.7% on the month with acceleration 2.02, GRID +4.2% and turning up, GEV +7.2%. The generation side has deflated: CEG -12.6% on the month, NLR -12.1% and at the 0.3rd percentile of 52 weeks, VST at the 4th, URA -10.1%. Falling power-price expectations hit the IPPs and barely touch the backlog names.
trades.trigger: Today GRID +2.1% and ETN +0.7% while CEG -2.0% and VST -1.6% on a strong tape — a clean, same-day divergence inside the same theme.
trades.stop: NLR/CEG outperform the pair by 7% or ETN loses its 50-day and acceleration flips negative.
trades.target: +10% on the spread over the quarter.

trades.name: Brazil over Mexico
trades.line: Long EWZ / short EWW — peso stress at z=2.7, Bovespa at 81st
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, dollar neutral; size half and add on any EWW bounce toward its 50-day.
trades.thesis: Mexico is the epicentre of the dollar squeeze: USDMXN z=2.72 with acceleration 2.20, EWW -8.1% on the month, rolling over, relative strength -8.9%/-10.5%. Brazil is the opposite tape — BVSP +2.2% on the week at the 81st percentile, EWZ +8.4% over three months with positive 3-month relative strength, and carry still intact. One LatAm book, two opposite directions.
trades.trigger: USDMXN made another high today (+0.7%) while EWZ closed +0.5% and MXX -0.6%.
trades.stop: USDMXN back under 17.60 (z under 1) with EWW outperforming EWZ by 5%.

trades.name: Japan, unhedged
trades.line: Long EWJ / Nikkei futures — chip-led, yen not collapsing
trades.expr: Long EWJ outright (or Nikkei 225 futures); leave yen exposure unhedged since USDJPY is -1.5% on the month.
trades.thesis: Japan is the cleanest way to own the global chip impulse with better valuation than US semis. Nikkei +3.30% to 68,957, +5.3% on the week, +37.0% YTD, relative strength versus the S&P turning up, EWJ at the 99th percentile of 52 weeks. Crucially the move is not a weak-yen artefact: USDJPY is -1.5% over a month with z=-0.74, so this is earnings and foreign inflow, not FX accounting.
trades.trigger: Today's +3.3% Nikkei close on Micron-led chip strength and Korean export data, with EWJ +1.1% and EWY +2.8% confirming the regional breadth.
trades.stop: Nikkei closes back below its 50-day or USDJPY breaks above 162 (disorderly yen) — the latter changes the character of the trade.

trades.name: Buy cheap index downside
trades.line: Long SPX put spread — VIX 15.6 vs MOVE +33% on the month
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPX 7,400/6,900 put spreads (roughly 4%/11% out of the money), or VIX Nov 20/30 call spreads; fund partially by selling 2-week upside calls.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for calm that the rest of the board does not support: VIX 15.64 at the 12th percentile, VIX3M at the 7th, SKEW -4.3% on the month — all while MOVE is +33.2% on the month, the 10y real yield is accelerating at 1.39, and RSP/SPY sits at the 3.6th percentile. A tape held up by four semis with the median stock rolling over is exactly where a 5% air pocket gets paid at a 2:1 premium.
trades.trigger: VIX -4.6% today on a day when the equal-weight/cap-weight ratio made a new 52-week relative low — vol compressing into deteriorating internals.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY turning up through its 50-day with HYG back above its 200-day — broadening would kill the convexity thesis; let the structure decay.
trades.target: 3-4x on the put spread on a 6-8% SPX drawdown; VIX above 24.

trades.name: Short the capital-markets complex
trades.line: Short BX and IAI — steep curve, still liquidating
trades.expr: Short BX outright; add short IAI as the diversified leg, or buy BX 3-month puts.
trades.thesis: The 3m10y curve is at the 98th percentile of the year, the classic green light for financials, and the group keeps being sold anyway: XLF -7.1% on the month with relative strength -7.9%, BX -16.9% (z=-1.76, 22nd percentile), GS -10.3%, IAI -7.6%, KIE z=-1.81. Private-credit and fee-engine marks are the pressure point when IG is -4.9% over three months and LQD is at the 3.6th percentile.
trades.trigger: On a +0.8% SPX day with KRE +0.7%, IAI still closed -0.3% and JPM -0.7% — the complex cannot hold a bid even on good days.
trades.stop: XLF relative strength turns up and BX reclaims its 200-day (10% above spot).
